proposals.statement:
theorem rowStep_agree_succ_two_iff (n x y : ℕ)
    (h : x % 2 ^ (n + 1) = y % 2 ^ (n + 1)) (hb : x.testBit n = true) :
    rowStep x % 2 ^ (n + 3) = rowStep y % 2 ^ (n + 3) ↔
      (x.testBit (n + 1) || x.testBit (n + 2)) = (y.testBit (n + 1) || y.testBit (n + 2)) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: THE FREE LEVEL, CHARACTERISED. After the board's own reductions the onset wall is: the agreement width between two rows reaches k+1 by time 2k. The only growth law the board owns is rowNat_return_succ_iff -- the width rises by one when the control bit is black -- and that law alone cannot reach the wall, by measurement rather than by feel. Measured over the seed's own rows at shift p = 16 (explorer/tessera_ladder.mjs, 5000 consecutive steps, width = the lowest bit where rows t and t+16 disagree): the control bit is black on 2022 of those 5000 steps, so a ladder counting only the +1 law gains width at slope 2.473, while the wall's budget is slope 2 -- over budget, so a reset-only ladder is not merely critical, it fails. The width actually gained is 3796, slope 1.317, because 1353 of the 2022 increments are jumps of two or more. This theorem is exactly when a jump of two happens. Once the control bit is black, bit n+2 of both successors is the negation of (bit n+1 OR bit n+2), so the two rows agree there as soon as those two ORs agree -- and an OR forgets information, so it agrees more often than a bit does (5/8 against 1/2 on uniform bits, measured). That coarsening is the free level a wall proof has to price, and it is Gnomon's 'a node whose loop is intact can still be forced, because its two drivers agree' (crystal 62) written as an iff. It strictly generalises the closed rowNat_return_succ_two, which is the single case where both rows are black at n+1, and unlike that node it holds for arbitrary starts -- which the board's own reduction leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_stepMod_preperiod requires, since it quantifies over every start and not only the seed's rows. Crystal 66's OR-to-XOR filter was run on this proposal before it was written down: replacing the two ORs by XORs makes the statement FALSE, checked in the kernel, so the claim is not blind to the term that is rule 30's whole difficulty.
proposals.disclaims: Does not prove the onset wall and gives no bound on anything. It says when one level is free, not how often -- and how often is exactly the open part. The slopes 2.473 and 1.317 are measured over 5000 steps at one shift on the seed's own rows and are not proved to persist; the 'black control' denominator here is 'bit W(t)-1 of row t is black', which is a different measurement from crystal 62's cascade and its 0.4993, so the two numbers should not be compared without saying that.

route.tactics:
have tb : ∀ r i : ℕ, (rowStep r).testBit i
      = xor (decide (2 ≤ i) && r.testBit (i - 2))
          ((decide (1 ≤ i) && r.testBit (i - 1)) || r.testBit i) := by
    intro r i
    have h4 : 4 * r = 2 ^ 2 * r := by norm_num
    have h2 : 2 * r = 2 ^ 1 * r := by norm_num
    unfold rowStep
    rw [h4, h2, Nat.testBit_xor, Nat.testBit_or, Nat.testBit_two_pow_mul,
      Nat.testBit_two_pow_mul]
  have miff : ∀ a b m : ℕ, a % 2 ^ m = b % 2 ^ m ↔ ∀ i < m, a.testBit i = b.testBit i := by
    intro a b m
    constructor
    · intro hh i hi
      have := congrArg (fun z => z.testBit i) hh
      simpa [Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow, hi] using this
    · intro hh
      apply Nat.eq_of_testBit_eq
      intro i
      rw [Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow, Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow]
      by_cases hi : i < m
      · simp [hi, hh i hi]
      · simp [hi]
  have hlow := (miff _ _ _).1 h
  have hby : y.testBit n = true := by rw [← hlow n (by omega)]; exact hb
  have hlow2 : ∀ i < n + 2, (rowStep x).testBit i = (rowStep y).testBit i := by
    intro i hi
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i (n + 1) with hi' | hi'
    · rw [tb, tb, hlow (i - 2) (by omega), hlow (i - 1) (by omega), hlow i (by omega)]
    · have hin : i = n + 1 := by omega
      subst hin
      have h1 : decide (1 ≤ n + 1) = true := by simp
      rw [tb, tb, show n + 1 - 1 = n by omega, hlow (n + 1 - 2) (by omega), h1,
        Bool.true_and, hb, hby]
      simp
  have htop : ((rowStep x).testBit (n + 2) = (rowStep y).testBit (n + 2)) ↔
      ((x.testBit (n + 1) || x.testBit (n + 2)) = (y.testBit (n + 1) || y.testBit (n + 2))) := by
    have h1 : decide (1 ≤ n + 2) = true := by simp
    have h2 : decide (2 ≤ n + 2) = true := by simp
    rw [tb, tb, show n + 2 - 1 = n + 1 by omega, show n + 2 - 2 = n by omega, h1, h2,
      Bool.true_and, Bool.true_and, Bool.true_and, Bool.true_and, hb, hby]
    generalize (x.testBit (n + 1) || x.testBit (n + 2)) = a
    generalize (y.testBit (n + 1) || y.testBit (n + 2)) = b
    cases a <;> cases b <;> decide
  rw [miff]
  constructor
  · intro hall
    exact htop.1 (hall (n + 2) (by omega))
  · intro hor i hi
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge i (n + 2) with hi' | hi'
    · exact hlow2 i hi'
    · have : i = n + 2 := by omega
      subst this
      exact htop.2 hor

proposals.statement:
theorem rowStep_agree_succ_iff (n x y : ℕ) (h : x % 2 ^ (n + 1) = y % 2 ^ (n + 1)) :
    rowStep x % 2 ^ (n + 2) = rowStep y % 2 ^ (n + 2) ↔
      (x.testBit n = true ∨ x % 2 ^ (n + 2) = y % 2 ^ (n + 2)) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: THE FRONTIER LAW, FOR EVERY START. This is rowNat_return_succ_iff with the seed taken out of it: the same iff, about two arbitrary numbers rather than about rows T and T+p of the single-seed picture. The board needs that form and cannot get it from the closed node, because the route the board actually reduced to is quantified over every start -- leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_stepMod_preperiod asks for a preperiod bound for every x < 2^(k+1), and stepMod_preperiod_of_odd likewise ranges over all x. Crystal 61, the connector's own first-ranked item, states the wall in exactly that all-starts shape and notes it is strictly stronger than the wall while mentioning no automaton. A proof along that route cannot cite rowNat_return_succ_iff at any step, since none of its numbers is a rowNat. Why it is true: bit n+1 of the successor is x(n-1) XOR (x(n) OR x(n+1)); the two lower bits are common by hypothesis, so the successors can only differ there, and a black bit n saturates the OR and forces agreement whatever bit n+1 holds. Together with rowStep_agree_succ_two_iff this is the complete one-step account of how an agreement frontier moves: this node says when it moves at all, that one says when it moves by two.

    unfold rowStep
    rw [h4, h2, Nat.testBit_xor, Nat.testBit_or, Nat.testBit_two_pow_mul,
      Nat.testBit_two_pow_mul]
  have miff : ∀ a b m : ℕ, a % 2 ^ m = b % 2 ^ m ↔ ∀ i < m, a.testBit i = b.testBit i := by
    intro a b m

    · intro hh i hi

    · intro hh
      apply Nat.eq_of_testBit_eq
      intro i
      rw [Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow, Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow]
      by_cases hi : i < m
      · simp [hi, hh i hi]
      · simp [hi]
  have hlow := (miff _ _ _).1 h
  have hbit : ((rowStep x).testBit (n + 1) = (rowStep y).testBit (n + 1)) ↔
      (x.testBit n = true ∨ x.testBit (n + 1) = y.testBit (n + 1)) := by
    have h1 : decide (1 ≤ n + 1) = true := by simp

    generalize y.testBit n = b
    generalize x.testBit (n + 1) = c

    · have : i = n + 1 := by omega
      subst this
      rw [hbit]

      · exact Or.inr (h1 (n + 1) (by omega))

proposals.statement:
theorem rowStep_agree_forward (n t x y : ℕ) (h : x % 2 ^ n = y % 2 ^ n) :
    rowStep^[t] x % 2 ^ n = rowStep^[t] y % 2 ^ n := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: AGREEMENT IS NEVER LOST, FOR EVERY START. rowNat_agree_forward says this about the seed's rows and is the reason an agreement front is monotone in time -- the wall's own description names it as one of the three blocks a decomposition should use. The all-starts route cannot cite it, for the same reason as the node above: none of its numbers is a rowNat. Every frontier argument opens by fixing the width already reached and then arguing about the next bit, and that is only meaningful if the width cannot shrink, so this is the standing hypothesis of the whole family rather than one step in it. There is direct evidence the board wants it public: the one-step congruence behind it, rowStep_mod_two_pow, has been privately re-declared in three separate closed proof files (RowNatModEqIterate, RowNatReturnSuccIff, LeftDiagonalOnsetLeIffRowNatReturn) and the bit-expansion testBit_rowStep in four, so no proof file can cite another's copy. The honest caveat on that count, per the caution in crystals about duplication: these files sit on the same brief chain and the copies may have been carried forward rather than independently derived, so the count is evidence that the fact is needed everywhere, not that four people each thought of it.

route.tactics:
have rs_mod : ∀ r m : ℕ, rowStep r % 2 ^ m = rowStep (r % 2 ^ m) % 2 ^ m := by
    intro r m
    have tb : ∀ s i : ℕ, (rowStep s).testBit i
        = xor (decide (2 ≤ i) && s.testBit (i - 2))
            ((decide (1 ≤ i) && s.testBit (i - 1)) || s.testBit i) := by
      intro s i
      have h4 : 4 * s = 2 ^ 2 * s := by norm_num
      have h2 : 2 * s = 2 ^ 1 * s := by norm_num
      unfold rowStep
      rw [h4, h2, Nat.testBit_xor, Nat.testBit_or, Nat.testBit_two_pow_mul,
        Nat.testBit_two_pow_mul]
    apply Nat.eq_of_testBit_eq
    intro i
    rw [Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow, Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow, tb, tb]
    by_cases hi : i < m
    · have h1 : i - 1 < m := by omega
      have h2 : i - 2 < m := by omega
      simp [Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow, hi, h1, h2]
    · simp [hi]
  induction t generalizing x y with
  | zero => simpa using h
  | succ t ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply, Function.iterate_succ_apply]
    exact ih _ _ (by rw [rs_mod, h, ← rs_mod])

proposals.statement:
theorem stepMod_iterate_eq_rowStep_mod (n t x : ℕ) :
    (stepMod n)^[t] (x % 2 ^ n) = rowStep^[t] x % 2 ^ n := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: THE JOINT BETWEEN THE BOARD'S TWO PACKED-ROW VEHICLES. The board now carries the onset wall in two different currencies and cannot convert between them for an arbitrary start. Its reductions are in stepMod -- leftDiagonal_onset_le_of_stepMod_preperiod, stepMod_preperiod_of_odd, stepMod_preperiod_of_return, stepMod_preperiod_le_of_le_11, stepMod_iterate_two_mul -- while every bitwise law about the frontier is naturally about rowStep, because truncating at n hides the very bits n+1 and n+2 that the two laws above read. rowNat_mod_eq_iterate is the only bridge on the board and it converts only the seed's own orbit, so an all-starts argument that proves its step lemmas in rowStep has no way to hand the result to the reduction that consumes it. This is that handover: the truncated orbit of a truncated start is the untruncated orbit truncated at the end. It is also the precise statement that rule 30's row map is a T-function in the sense crystal 60 uses -- information moves only upward through the bits, so the levels form a tower rather than unrelated finite systems -- which is asserted in the docstring of stepMod and proved nowhere.

have rs_mod : ∀ r m : ℕ, rowStep r % 2 ^ m = rowStep (r % 2 ^ m) % 2 ^ m := by
    intro r m
    have tb : ∀ s i : ℕ, (rowStep s).testBit i
        = xor (decide (2 ≤ i) && s.testBit (i - 2))
            ((decide (1 ≤ i) && s.testBit (i - 1)) || s.testBit i) := by
      intro s i
      have h4 : 4 * s = 2 ^ 2 * s := by norm_num
      have h2 : 2 * s = 2 ^ 1 * s := by norm_num
      unfold rowStep
      rw [h4, h2, Nat.testBit_xor, Nat.testBit_or, Nat.testBit_two_pow_mul,
        Nat.testBit_two_pow_mul]
    apply Nat.eq_of_testBit_eq
    intro i
    rw [Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow, Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow, tb, tb]
    by_cases hi : i < m
    · have h1 : i - 1 < m := by omega
      have h2 : i - 2 < m := by omega
      simp [Nat.testBit_mod_two_pow, hi, h1, h2]
    · simp [hi]
  induction t generalizing x with
  | zero => simp
  | succ t ih =>
    rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply, Function.iterate_succ_apply]
    have hs : stepMod n (x % 2 ^ n) = rowStep x % 2 ^ n := by
      unfold stepMod; rw [← rs_mod]

proposals.statement:
theorem periodicFrom_gcd (f : ℕ → Bool) (p q N : ℕ)
    (hpN : PeriodicFrom f p N) (hqN : PeriodicFrom f q N) :
    PeriodicFrom f (Nat.gcd p q) N := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: THE MISSING COMBINER, AND THE REASON THE PERIOD WALL IS ABOUT POWERS OF TWO. The board can multiply periods (periodicFrom_mul), move a period to an earlier onset (periodicFrom_trans_period), and divide a period from zero by minimality (minimalPeriod_dvd), but it cannot combine two periods of the same sequence. That is the operation the period wall needs. leftDiagonal_period_le asks for a period at most k+1; leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_pow independently supplies the period 2^k. Their gcd is a power of two and is at most the smaller of the two, so this node is exactly what turns 'diagonal k has some period at most k+1' into 'diagonal k has a POWER-OF-TWO period at most k+1' -- and that upgrade is what makes the periods of the first n diagonals totally ordered by divisibility, hence lets one common period serve them all without an lcm blowing past n. Crystal 56 states the wall's honest form as a claim about the doubling positions k_n, which is a claim about powers of two; nothing on the board currently licenses reading it that way. It is used directly by leftDiagonal_period_le_iff_rowNat_period below and is the only step of that node that is not bookkeeping. Why it is true: periods from N are closed under subtraction, because f (n + (a-b)) = f (n + (a-b) + b) = f (n + a) = f n, and Euclid's algorithm is repeated subtraction; the positivity hypotheses you might expect are not needed, since gcd 0 0 = 0 and period 0 is trivially true.

route.tactics:
have hsub : ∀ a b : ℕ, b ≤ a → PeriodicFrom f a N → PeriodicFrom f b N →
      PeriodicFrom f (a - b) N := by
    intro a b hba ha hb n hn
    have h1 : f (n + (a - b) + b) = f (n + (a - b)) := hb _ (by omega)
    have h2 : n + (a - b) + b = n + a := by omega
    rw [h2] at h1
    rw [← h1]
    exact ha n hn
  have hmul : ∀ a : ℕ, PeriodicFrom f a N → ∀ m : ℕ, PeriodicFrom f (m * a) N := by
    intro a ha m
    induction m with
    | zero => intro n hn; simp
    | succ m ihm =>
      intro n hn
      have e : n + (m + 1) * a = n + m * a + a := by ring
      rw [e, ha _ (le_trans hn (Nat.le_add_right _ _)), ihm n hn]
  have key : ∀ a b : ℕ, PeriodicFrom f a N → PeriodicFrom f b N →
      PeriodicFrom f (Nat.gcd a b) N := by
    intro a
    induction a using Nat.strong_induction_on with
    | _ a ih =>
      intro b ha hb
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos a with rfl | hpos
      · simpa using hb
      · have hdm : a * (b / a) + b % a = b := Nat.div_add_mod b a
        have hle : a * (b / a) ≤ b := by omega
        have hbmod : PeriodicFrom f (b % a) N := by
          have hstep := hsub b (a * (b / a)) hle hb
            (by rw [Nat.mul_comm]; exact hmul a ha (b / a))
          have : b - a * (b / a) = b % a := by omega
          rwa [this] at hstep
        rw [Nat.gcd_rec]
        exact ih (b % a) (Nat.mod_lt _ hpos) a hbmod ha
  exact key p q hpN hqN

proposals.statement:
theorem leftDiagonal_period_le_iff_rowNat_period :
    (∀ k : ℕ, ∃ p, 0 < p ∧ p ≤ k + 1 ∧ ∃ N, PeriodicFrom (leftDiagonal k) p N) ↔
      (∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → ∃ p, 0 < p ∧ p ≤ n ∧
        ∃ T, rowNat T % 2 ^ n = rowNat (T + p) % 2 ^ n) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: THE PERIOD WALL WITH NO AUTOMATON IN IT. This is the one recommendation of the attack document of 2026-09-09 ('Two unexplained numbers from today's kernel checks', section 4) that has not landed: its author names it as what they would seed first, 'the only one of the four that puts something new UNDER a wall', because it moves leftDiagonal_period_le into the same N-only arithmetic frame where leftDiagonal_onset_le now lives. That matters concretely rather than aesthetically. Both walls are now claims about the orbit of a single number under r -> 4r XOR (2r OR r); one script measures both, one induction could attack both, and the whole packed-row toolkit the board landed on 2026-09-10 and the four nodes above become available to the period wall, which currently has none of it. Why the equivalence holds. Backward is one line: leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_of_rowNat_agree_any at k = n-1 turns the congruence into a period p <= n = (n-1)+1 for diagonal n-1. Forward is the work, and it has a route that needs no maximum over onsets. For each j < n take the given period p_j <= j+1 and the power-of-two period 2^j from leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_pow; periodicFrom_gcd makes q_j = gcd(p_j, 2^j) a period, a power of two, and at most p_j <= n. periodicFrom_trans_period then moves every one of them onto the uniform onset 2^j <= 2^n that leftDiagonal_periodicFrom_pow already supplies, so no max is needed. Now take q = 2 ^ Nat.log 2 n, the largest power of two at most n: every q_j is a power of two at most n, hence divides q, so periodicFrom_mul puts all n diagonals on the single period q <= n. Finally leftDiagonal_eq_rowNat_testBit reads those n agreements off as the n low bits of rows T and T+q at T = 2^n + n, and Nat.eq_of_testBit_eq assembles the congruence. Measured: the arithmetic side holds for every n from 1 to 700, and the least power of two that works steps up at n = 1, 4, 9, 30, 401 -- which is exactly the known doubling depths 3, 8, 29, 400 shifted by one, an independent reproduction of NKS p. 871 and of crystal 57's staircase from this statement alone (explorer/tessera_ladder.mjs).
proposals.disclaims: Proves neither wall and bounds nothing. It is a change of vocabulary: it says the period wall and an arithmetic statement about one integer orbit are the same claim, and both remain open. It carries no witness on purpose -- the left-hand side is a quantifier over all k with two unbounded existentials inside it and is not checkable at any finite range, and leftDiagonal is evolve, which gives out near t = 18. The arithmetic side alone was checked to n = 700 and that is reported above as what it is, evidence about one side of an iff.
